World.title: CHED postpones pilot test of reframed GE after coming under fire
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

The announcement comes a day after teachers, students, and advocacy groups filed a petition asking the Commission on Higher Education not to proceed with its proposal to reduce general education units

MANILA, Philippines – The Commission on Higher Education (CHED) will not conduct pilot testing of the proposed reframed general education (GE) curriculum in 2026 as it vowed to review more comments from stakeholders.

The announcement came a day after teachers, students, and advocacy groups filed a consolidated petition and separate position papers asking CHED not to proceed with its proposal to reduce GE units to 18 from the current 36.

CHED Chairperson Shirley Agrupis, in a press conference on Wednesday evening, May 13, said the pilot implementation of the overhauled GE curriculum will be moved to 2028 instead.

“This is to give us time…to analyze and study well the different manifestations because we understand where they are coming from,” Agrupis said.

The decision was the result of the meeting between CHED, the Department of Education, Second Congressional Commission on Education, and Teacher Education Council on Wednesday afternoon.

The four government bodies also decided to create an inter-agency technical working group to examine the position papers this year. They are open to receiving more submissions until June 15.

As of now, over 250 higher education institutions have submitted their stances. Agrupis said many of the demands are “worth considering.”

She acknowledged that critics have questioned the bid of the CHED Technical Panel for General Education to lump together Philippine history with the Rizal course, and to remove ethics as a stand-alone subject in the reframed curriculum.

Edizon Fermin, who leads the technical panel, also explained why they initially proposed launching the pilot testing in school year 2026-2027, which begins in August.

“We thought it was propitious that we try it out do‘n sa ilalabas na teacher education curriculum. So parang dalawa po ‘yung pagkakataon na hinahabol ng CHED: Makita ‘yung posibilidad to reframe GE at the same time we are reframing teacher education,” Fermin said.

(We thought it was propitious that we try it out along with the reframed teacher education curriculum. So CHED was eyeing two opportunities: To see the possibility of reframing GE at the same time we are reframing teacher education.)

In 2018, CHED cut GE units from 60 to 36 following the implementation of the K to 12 program in the country. – Rappler.com

World.title: Marcos: Gov’t didn’t swarm Senate; no orders to arrest Dela Rosa
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

MESSAGE FROM THE PRESIDENT. Malacañang Palace releases a taped statement from President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. late May 13, 2026, hours after gunshots were heard in the Senate after it went on lockdown.

MANILA, Philippines – President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said late Wednesday, May 13, that there were no standing orders from himself or any other officials in the executive to arrest Senator Ronald dela Rosa, the former police chief who faces a warrant from the International Criminal Court over his alleged role in former president Rodrigo Duterte’s war on drugs.

Marcos’ statement, delivered through a recorded message that was then sent to the media, came hours after gunshots were heard at the Philippine Senate after the premises were ordered locked down.

Marcos’ top security officials, including Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla and Philippine National Police (PNP) chief Jose Melencio Nartatez, had both gone to the Senate after shots were heard ringing through the Senate’s right wing.

The President said he had been monitoring the situation in Pasay City and confirmed with both Nartatez and National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) chief Melvin Matibag that no shots were fired from their personnel and that neither the PNP nor the NBI was trying to serve the arrest warrant against Dela Rosa.

Newly installed Senate President Alan Peter Cayetano, in his first Facebook live of the night, accused the NBI of entering the Senate and claimed that the Senate was “under attack.” He would later say that it was an “alleged attack” on the upper chamber. Marcos’ estranged older sister, Senator Imee Marcos, told reporters after the chaos had been settled, that the Senate was under “siege.”

The Philippine President said that was not the case: “Kalma lang po. Asahan ninyo ang gobyerno ninyo hindi gagawin ito (Please remain calm. Trust that your government will not do this),” he said.

Marcos said he had spoken to Cayetano and agreed that “the thing to do now is to tell our people all to calm down and we will get to the bottom of this.”

Both the Senate and the PNP are set to hold parallel investigations into the matter.

“Aalamin natin kung sino ang gumawa nitong gulo na ito — ito ba ay talagang engkuwentro lang, ito ba ay kasama sa destab or nagsisimula ng gulo? Kailangan po nating malaman ‘yan,” Marcos added.

(We will find out who caused this chaos. Was this really just an encounter? Is this part of attempts to destabilize the government or trigger chaos? We need to know the truth.)

Marcos was once a member of the Senate before losing his 2016 bid for the vice presidency, then winning his 2022 presidential bid.

Dela Rosa, who headed the PNP at the beginning of Duterte’s bloody drug war, was once a close ally of Marcos and even campaigned for and alongside him in the 2022 elections. Marcos was then a close ally of the Dutertes, primarily through then-running mate and now-Vice President Sara Duterte.

In February 2025, the Marcos administration facilitated the arrest of the older Duterte, who now awaits trial for crimes against humanity at the ICC. Marcos then explained that the Philippines had to comply with the ICC warrant against his predecessor, citing the country’s international obligations. – Rappler.com

World.title: Once Duterte’s target, Jed Mabilog now joins DILG
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

BACK. Former Iloilo City mayor Jed Mabilog, who fled the country after he was included in former president Rodrigo Duterte's drug list, attends the House quad committee hearing on September 19, 2024.

Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla says that Jed Mabilog's experience with injustice will fuel his desire to 'level the playing field' in local governance

CEBU, Philippines – President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. appointed former Iloilo City mayor Jed Mabilog as undersecretary for public safety at the Department of the Interior and Local Government on Wednesday, May 13.

Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla administered the oath to the newly-appointed official on Wednesday morning. Mabilog confirmed this in a statement sent to the media on Wednesday evening.

“I likewise pledge my full support in advancing the vision and programs of President Marcos under the Bagong Pilipinas agenda,” Mabilog said.

In August 2017, Mabilog left the country after then-president Rodrigo Duterte accused him of being involved in the illegal drug trade happening in Iloilo and swore to put him on his list of high-profile drug suspects who were being killed by authorities.

Prior to his departure abroad, Duterte announced the reassignment of controversial Chief Inspector Jovie Espenido to Iloilo. Espenido was given the role of chasing after mayors with alleged links to illegal drugs

Espenido’s arrival in Iloilo raised concerns for Mabilog’s safety as the police officer was previously involved in operations that resulted in the deaths of two mayors accused of being “narco-politicians.”

For seven years, the former Iloilo City mayor went into a self-imposed exile in the United States where he sought asylum. While abroad, the Office of the Ombudsman sought the dismissal of Mabilog in October 2017 for having a pecuniary interest in a towing services company that the city government contracted.

Mabilog fought his dismissal up to the Supreme Court in July 2019. It ended with the High Court upholding the dismissal. The Office of the Ombudsman filed the accompanying criminal graft charges before the Sandiganbayan and the Lapu-Lapu Regional Trial Court in 2023.

In 2024, Mabilog returned to the Philippines and posted bail before both courts. In January 2025, President Marcos Jr. granted executive clemency to Mabilog in relation to his administrative case.

“The injustice he went through will fuel his desire to level the playing field in local governance. Not revenge but reform,” Remulla said in a GMA News Online article.

Amid Senate chaos

Mabilog’s appointment came around several hours before chaos at the Philippine Senate erupted — gunshots were fired inside the Senate building on Wednesday night.

This all happened amid the controversy over the presence of Senator Ronald dela Rosa in the Senate building. In a Facebook live on Wednesday afternoon, Dela Rosa said he received information that agents from the National Bureau of Investigation and police planned to arrest him there.

It can be recalled that Dela Rosa, who was then-Philippine National Police (PNP) chief during the first two years of the Duterte administration, allegedly called Mabilog who was abroad to come home, according to Mabilog’s affidavit presented during a House quad committee hearing on September 19, 2024.

In the same affidavit, Mabilog recalled that shortly after the call with Dela Rosa, an unnamed PNP general called him and warned him not to return to the country.

Mabilog shared what the police general said — that his life was in danger and that if he returns, he would be forced to label an opposition senator and a former presidential candidate as drug lords. – Rappler.com

World.title: Gunshots fired during Senate lockdown; officials say no arrest yet for Bato
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

'CLEAR THE HALLWAY'. Senate security personnel and police officers ask members of the media to leave the building after gunshots were heard, on May 13, 2026.

(1st UPDATE) National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag says they are not enforcing any arrest warrants on Wednesday night, May 13

MANILA, Philippines – Gunshots were fired within the premises of the Senate building after it went into another lockdown on Wednesday night, May 13.

The lockdown comes hours after the Supreme Court did not provide immediate relief to Senator Bato dela Rosa, who is seeking a temporary restraining order against a warrant issued against him by the International Criminal Court.

Past 7 pm on Wednesday, reporters were told to leave the Senate building ahead of the impending lockdown. Reporters also saw soldiers inside the building around that time. Some reporters were even blocked from going to the Senate’s fifth floor, where Dela Rosa’s office is located.

At around 7:45 pm, reporters heard multiple gunshots being fired inside the Senate premises. A few minutes before gunshots were heard, Marines detailed to the Senate fell into formation in the right wing of the Senate building. Before proceeding, the personnel — wearing bulletproof vests — cocked their long firearms.

Reporters were asked to vacate the building right after.

Play Video

Senate President Alan Peter Cayetano later went live on Facebook to confirm that gunshots were fired as senators were holding a caucus.

“This is the Senate of the Philippines…. Sa lahat ng nakikinig (To everyone who’s listening) — PNP [Philippine National Police], DILG [Department of the Interior and Local Government] — what is happening? NBI [National Bureau of Investigation], what is happening? Why are we under attack here?” Cayetano said.

Senate Secretary Mark Leandro Mendoza, speaking to reporters, said armed personnel — allegedly from the NBI — were the first to fire shots but said the Senate premises were still “safe.” NBI Director Melvin Matibag, however, disputed this, saying NBI personnel in the vicinity of the Senate did not have firearms with them.

Matibag also said they were not enforcing any warrants on Wednesday night.

“Ang mabigat po diyan, wala pang imbestigasyon, nagtuturo na (What’s worse is that they’re already pointing fingers without a proper investigation).”

Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said no casualties were reported after the incident. He also said he went to the Senate to ensure the safety of senators and not to enforce any warrant against Dela Rosa.

PNP chief Jose Melencio Nartatez also arrived on Wednesday night to secure the Senate premises after Senate Sergeant-at-Arms Mao Aplasca earlier called him asking for help. He said no PNP personnel fired shots, but that an investigation was forthcoming.

In another Facebook live, Cayetano said both President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. rang him to “assure” senators that the gunshots did not come from government forces.

Dela Rosa is still inside the Senate building as of 11 pm Wednesday, according to his lawyer Jimmy Bondoc. Remulla also earlier confirmed this.

Initial reports on the shooting indicated that “armed men” entered the Senate building, which prompted the Senate Sergeant-at-Arms to fire warning shots. The armed men reportedly fired back. No one was arrested in the aftermath of the shooting, and no suspect has so far been identified.

Play Video

During the lockdown, articles of impeachment against Vice President Sara Duterte were also delivered to the Senate past 8 pm on Wednesday. – Rappler.com

World.title: PH may surrender suspects to international court, says DOJ
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

BATO. Senator Ronald 'Bato' dela Rosa speaks to members of the media, at the Senate on May 13, 2026.

'Under [Republic Act No.] 9851, we may surrender a suspected or arrested person in the Philippines to the appropriate international court or tribunal. The other mode is extradition,' the DOJ says

MANILA, Philippines – The Philippine Department of Justice (DOJ) on Wednesday, May 13, reiterated that the Philippine government can surrender suspects to international courts, based on local law.

“Under [Republic Act No.] 9851, we may surrender a suspected or arrested person in the Philippines to the appropriate international court or tribunal. The other mode is extradition,” DOJ spokesperson Prosecutor Rafael Martinez told reporters.

The DOJ issued the clarification after it was asked if local law allows the Philippine government to cooperate with the International Criminal Court (ICC). The tribunal recently unsealed its warrant against Senator Bato dela Rosa.

Dela Rosa, the first Philippine National Police (PNP) chief who implemented former president Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war, is facing a warrant after he was found to be allegedly criminally liable for crimes against humanity. This case covers the alleged killings under the war on drugs and by the Davao Death Squad.

The National Bureau of Investigation tried implementing the warrant on Monday, May 11, but failed.

As of writing, Dela Rosa remains in the Senate to evade arrest in line with the Senate’s supposed “no arrest” tradition within its compound. Law experts and former lawmakers, however, said this has limitations and that Dela Rosa may be arrested within Senate premises.

Aside from this, some senator allies of Dela Rosa are claiming that the former PNP chief can only be arrested based on a local warrant.

The premise is both problematic and unnecessary because of Republic Act No. 9851’s (RA 9851) application on suspects who are subjects of an international warrant.

RA 9851 or the “Philippine Act on Crimes Against International Humanitarian Law, Genocide, and Other Crimes Against Humanity” is a local law that transformed international criminal law into a domestic law.

Its section 17 states: “Instead, the authorities may surrender or extradite suspected or accused persons in the Philippines to the appropriate international court, if any, or to another State pursuant to the applicable extradition laws and treaties.”

This was the same basis used by the Marcos administration when it arrested Duterte in 2025.

“Basically domestic law is allowing local authorities to step back and allow another court (regional or international) to step in. So, to that extent, it’s in perfect compliance with RA No. 9851, which has already provided for this possibility,” international lawyer Priya Pillai said in 2025. – Rappler.com

World.title: Imus City LGU extends 4-day workweek until December
World.content:
The local government of Imus City in Cavite announced Thursday, May 14, 2026, that it will continue implementing the four-day compressed workweek until December this year. INQUIRER FILES

LUCENA CITY, Quezon – The local government of Imus City in Cavite announced Thursday that it will continue implementing the four-day compressed workweek until December this year.

In a public advisory in Filipino posted on its Facebook page, the city government said Mayor Alex “AA” L. Advincula signed Executive Order No. 029 on May 11, extending the implementation of the four-day workweek in the Imus City government until Dec. 25, 2026.

READ: Four-day workweek starts in some gov’t offices

Article continues after this 

“The extension of the four-day compressed workweek was prompted by the extreme heat and the continuing instability in petroleum product prices,” the local government explained.

Under the order, local government offices will remain open from Monday to Thursday, from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., to ensure uninterrupted delivery of public services.

But offices involved in health services, disaster response, and other essential operations are exempt from the directive and required to maintain continuous operations for public welfare.

Since March, many government offices have adopted the four-day workweek arrangement as part of energy-saving measures after President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. implemented the workweek scheme for executive branch offices to reduce energy costs.

READ: Four-day workweek: Where is the evidence?

Article continues after this 

The temporary scheme is also intended to reduce fuel consumption amid rising global oil prices linked to escalating tensions in the Middle East following attacks by Israel, backed by the United States, on Iran.

The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) earlier issued guidelines to implement the four-day workweek.

Article continues after this 

Under the guidelines, a flexitime arrangement may be observed between 7 a.m. and 8 a.m. for arrival, and 6 p.m. and 7 p.m. for departure, provided employees complete 10 working hours per day.

Employees reporting after 8 a.m. will be considered late, while Friday, Saturday, and Sunday are designated as rest days./coa

World.title: HEAT INDEX WATCH: Six Calabarzon areas face dangerous levels
World.content:
INQUIRER file image

LUCENA CITY, Quezon – At least six areas in the Calabarzon (Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, Rizal, Quezon) region are expected to experience dangerous heat index levels on Thursday and Friday, May 14 and 15, amid the continuing extreme heat.

In its 5 p.m. forecast issued Wednesday, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said Sangley Point in Cavite City, Cavite is forecast to register a heat index of 44 degrees Celsius on Thursday and 45°C on Friday.

Cavite City has been experiencing dangerous heat conditions in recent days, with the heat index reaching as high as 45°C on April 27.

Article continues after this 

Pagasa also forecast that Tanauan City in Batangas, as well as the towns of Alabat and Infanta in Quezon, will record a heat index of 43°C on both Thursday and Friday.

Meanwhile, Tayabas City in Quezon and Los Baños in Laguna are expected to register 42°C during the same period.

The weather bureau classifies heat index values ranging from 42°C to 51°C under the “danger” category, warning that prolonged exposure to extreme heat may cause heat cramps, heat exhaustion, and heat stroke.

Pagasa explained that the heat index reflects the level of discomfort felt by the human body due to the combined effects of air temperature and humidity.

The agency added that elevated heat index levels are likely to persist as the dry season continues, with peak heat conditions usually occurring from midday until late afternoon.

Article continues after this 

The Department of Health (DOH) urged residents to stay hydrated, avoid prolonged exposure to direct sunlight, and take preventive measures against heat-related illnesses amid the continuing high heat index conditions.

The DOH also advised the public to seek immediate medical attention in suspected cases of heat stroke.

Article continues after this 

Heat stroke is considered a medical emergency. The body temperature of a person suffering from heat stroke can rapidly rise to 106 degrees Fahrenheit or higher, potentially causing serious damage to the brain, heart, and kidneys. /jpv

World.title: NGCP warns of possible brownouts as grids hit red, yellow alert levels
World.content:
The NGCP transmission lines (Photo from NGCP’s Facebook page)

MANILA, Philippines – Brownouts may occur as the Luzon and Visayas grids were again placed under red and yellow alert on Thursday due to insufficient power supply and thin operating reserves, the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP) said.

The NGCP explained that a red alert is issued when “power supply is insufficient to meet consumer demand and the transmission grid’s regulating requirement.”

A yellow alert, meanwhile, is declared when the “operating margin is insufficient to meet the transmission grid’s contingency requirement.”

Article continues after this 

In an advisory issued at 8 a.m., NGCP said the Luzon grid will be under red alert from 4 p.m. to 10 p.m., while yellow alert status will be in effect from 3 p.m. to 4 p.m. and again from 10 p.m. to 11 p.m.

The Luzon grid recorded an available capacity of 12,479 megawatts (MW), against a peak demand of 12,595 MW.

According to NGCP, “17 plants are on forced outage since March 2026, 3 since 2025, 2 since 2024, and 1 plant out since 2019; while 14 plants are running on derated capacities.”

These outages and reduced capacities resulted in a total of 4,242.5 MW unavailable to the Luzon grid.

READ: Brownouts loom as NGCP raises red alert over Luzon, Visayas

Article continues after this 

Meanwhile, the Visayas grid was also placed under red alert from 4 p.m. to 9 p.m., with yellow alert raised from 3 p.m. to 4 p.m. and from 9 p.m. to 11 p.m.

The Visayas grid posted an available capacity of 2,413 MW, lower than the projected peak demand of 2,541 MW.

Article continues after this 

According to NGCP, “11 plants are on forced outage since March 2026, 4 since 2025, 2 since 2024, 2 since 2023, and 1 plant out since 2021; while 12 are running on derated capacities, for a total of 866.7MW unavailable to the grid.” /jpv

World.title: Magnitude 5.3 quake jolts Cagayan; aftershocks expected – Phivolcs
World.content:
Phivolcs map shows the epicenter of the magnitude 5.3 tectonic earthquake that struck 32 kilometers northwest of Dalupiri Island in Calayan, Cagayan early Thursday, May 14, 2026. Image from DOST / Phivolcs FB page

MANILA, Philippines — A magnitude 5.3 earthquake struck the waters northwest off Dalupiri Island in Calayan, Cagayan early Thursday morning, state seismologists said.

According to the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology’s (Phivolcs) latest advisory, no damage is expected from the earthquake, but aftershocks may occur.

READ: Magnitude 5.3 quake hits waters off Cagayan on Saturday, July 19

Article continues after this 

The tectonic quake occurred at 6:01 a.m. and was located 32 kilometers northwest of Dalupiri Island in Calayan, Cagayan.

The earthquake had a depth of focus of 7 kilometers.

Instrumental Intensity I was recorded at Batac and Bacarra in Ilocos Norte and City of Vigan and Narvacan in Ilocos Sur.

Phivolcs said, moreover, that reported intensities were as follows:

Intensity V – Calayan, Cagayan

Intensity IV – Pasuquin, Pagudpud and Burgos in Ilocos Norte

Intensity III – City of Laoag, San Nicolas and Bacarra in Ilocos Norte and Aparri in Cagayan

Intensity II – Pinili, Ilocos Norte

According to Phivolcs, under Intensity V, shaking is generally felt by most people indoors and outdoors, causing some residents to run outside and light objects to fall or overturn. /jpv

World.title: Cloudy skies, isolated rain showers to prevail Thursday – Pagasa
World.content:
Satellite image from the state weather bureau shows pattern of cloudy skies. DOST / Pagasa

MANILA, Philippines – Cloudy skies with isolated rain showers are expected this Thursday as localized thunderstorms continue to affect parts of the country, the state weather bureau said.

According to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa), the low pressure area (LPA), formerly called tropical cyclone “Caloy”, was last spotted 685 kilometers east of Virac, Catanduanes as of 3 a.m. Thursday.

READ: LPA may dissipate by weekend; fair weather expected

Article continues after this 

Pagasa weather specialist Loriedin de la Cruz-Galicia said although the LPA is inside the Philippine area of responsibility, the LPA has no direct effect on the country.

“Sa ngayon ay localized thunderstorms po ang pwedeng magdulot ng mga panandaliang pagbuhos ng ulan sa ilang bahagi ng bansa,” de la Cruz-Galicia said in Pagasa’s latest weather briefing.

(“At present, localized thunderstorms may bring brief rain showers in some parts of the country,”)

Metro Manila and the rest of the country may continue to experience generally fair weather with partly cloudy to cloudy skies, although isolated rain showers or thunderstorms remain possible, especially during the afternoon and evening.

The weather bureau also said warm and humid conditions may persist across the country.

Article continues after this 

Meanwhile, state weather forecasters also warned of danger level heat indices (42 to 51°C) in several areas nationwide.

Heat index is the apparent heat or “feels-like” temperature which says how hot it feels to the human body when humidity is factored in with the air temperature.

Article continues after this 

On Wednesday, the heat index in Metro Manila reached 43°C, while Butuan City, Agusan del Norte and Hinatuan, Surigao del Sur recorded the highest heat index at 47°C.

READ: HEAT INDEX WATCH: 49 areas to reach ‘danger’ level on Thursday, May 14

World.title: Lawyer urges public to track how Sara Duterte impeach case is resolved
World.content:
Romeo Macalintal FILE PHOTO

MANILA, Philippines — An election lawyer said Thursday that the public should focus on how Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial will be resolved, rather than whether it will even begin, noting that the majority of the current senators are allied with the Dutertes.

Atty. Romulo Macalintal shared his sentiments amid concerns raised by legal academicians, professors and even church officials on the current Senate leadership’s readiness to “forthwith” convene as an impeachment court once it has received the articles of impeachment against Duterte.

READ: House: ‘Articles of impeachment’ vs Sara Duterte sent to Senate

Article continues after this 

For Macalintal, it is unlikely for newly installed Senate President Alan Peter Cayetano, who he described as a seasoned lawyer and veteran politician, to once again delay the convening of the impeachment court as doing so would not only invite a potential constitutional challenge, but also trigger a massive political backlash from the public.

Instead, Macalintal said that the more likely possibility is that Duterte’s legal team will include in her “answer a motion to dismiss the case” or a motion to quash the articles of impeachment, which he explained may not be explicitly provided by the rules of procedure on impeachment, but not prohibited either.

The lawyer pointed out that under current rules, such a motion would only require a simple majority vote or at least 13 senators.

“This is the same number of votes that secured the current Senate leadership. Given these numbers, the possibility of an early dismissal is a significant legal factor to consider,” said Macalintal.

“Hence, we should not focus solely on whether the Impeachment Court convenes ‘forthwith’. Instead, we must hope that the case is not dismissed on a mere technicality or the sheer power of the majority,” he added.

Article continues after this 

According to Macalintal, Duterte’s impeachment case must be decided based strictly on the evidence and the law, with the prosecution relying on the strength of its own evidence not simply on the weakness of the defense.

“With known allies now holding the reins of the Senate, the public must remain alert to the procedural strategies that could abbreviate these proceedings,” said Macalintal.

Article continues after this 

“Vigilance is necessary to ensure that the process remains transparent and substantive. Remember: ‘Forewarned is forearmed’,” he added.

Duterte is set to face the Senate impeachment court after the House of Representatives impeached her for the second time—a first for any government official in the country’s history.

World.title: Civil registry corrections made easier – PSA
World.content:
MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) has made petitions for corrections of civil registry data—from names, gender to date of birth—easier with the launch on Tuesday of a new digital system.

The Administrative Petition for Correction Automated System (Apcas) is designed to streamline the processing of these petitions covered under Republic Act No. 9048 and RA 10172.

Article continues after this 

This will reduce processing time by at least 80 percent for up to 180,000 requests annually.

READ: PSA: 12M national ID cards up for delivery in 2026

RA 9048 allows the civil registrar to correct clerical or typographical errors and change the first name or nickname of a person. This was later amended by RA 10172 to also include corrections in the day and month of birth, as well as the sex of a person.

Introduced in 2024

Apcas was first piloted in 2024 in selected regions. As of April 2026, the system has already processed nearly 6,000 petitions across 201 local civil registry offices (LCROs).

READ: PSA launches e-certificate service for birth, death, marriage registry

Article continues after this 

“Our vision for our country’s civil registration system is to establish a fully integrated, end-to-end digital ecosystem that streamlines processes, improves coordination across institutions, and ensures faster, more reliable service delivery,” PSA Undersecretary Claire Dennis Mapa said.

Reduced processing time

“By transitioning from manual administrative procedures to a streamlined digital workflow, Apcas empowers our local civil registry offices and our partners in local government units, including municipal and city civil registrars, to process petitions more efficiently, accurately, and securely,” he added.

Article continues after this 

According to Mapa, Apcas was developed in response to the high volume of correction petitions, which reach around 150,000 to 180,000 annually. Prior to the system’s rollout, these requests were processed manually.

The new system significantly reduces processing steps from 12 to 6, covering LCRO processing, screening at the PSA provincial office, case assignment, initial review, final review, and annotation processing.

Apcas also strengthens data security through a secure virtual private network and multifactor authentication to protect sensitive personal information.

Meanwhile, a gender-inclusive feature allows users to attach medical certification for changes in sex classification where applicable.
